notes: Large-source-unit check: `עַל־דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר` → *because* is genuinely indivisible — no morpheme owns a part of the one English word and none of its lexemes is written — so rule 6's first-token fallback supplies the anchor. Heading on the construct `דְּבַר` under rule 23 was the competing reading.
The second *because* answers to the written `אֲשֶׁר` of its own clause (rule 55), and the waw beside it keeps only the *and*.
Both object markers are `unrepresented`; the ASV writes its objects bare (rule 16).
